reason: Fruit gives the tree dwellers a useful place to find and potentially remember.
expectation: The tree dwellers will find food that could help establish a remembered place.

effect: Returning fruit has no available combination, so I need another way to engage the tree dwellers.
reaction: The failed attempt was a little surprising given the food-and-memory goal.
reason: Inspecting the tree dwellers should reveal which available object can start their story.
expectation: The report will identify compatible objects, and may automatically perform a sole available operation.

effect: Eyes transformed the tree dwellers into Attention, giving me a new starting point for the memory and warning goals.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified how to begin.
reason: Attention could lead in several directions, so checking its partners is more useful than guessing.
expectation: The report will show what Attention can combine with and may automatically perform a sole operation.

effect: Attention can connect either to danger or to seasonal change, suggesting paths toward the two goals.
reaction: The two distinct options make the next choice clearer.
reason: Seasons seem relevant to remembering when and where to return.
expectation: This may establish a memory of a place that changes with the seasons.

alternatives.reason: That could instead begin the warning path.

effect: Attention and Seasons created Memory, providing a likely route to the return goal.
reaction: The distinction between mythic arrival and memory's varied histories is useful.
reason: A remembered food source could give experience a practical role in returning to a place.
expectation: Memory and the fruit may lead the creature back to a familiar food source.

alternatives.reason: Checking its partners would avoid a guess, but the fruit seems relevant to the goal.

effect: Memory and fruit produced a learned path and completed the return goal; the warning goal remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see memory guide a return to food that is not yet visible.
reason: Attention was also compatible with Predator and prey, which looks like the clearest route toward a warning.
expectation: This will begin a response to danger that could lead to a shared warning.

effect: Attention and predator–prey encounters produced Fear, suggesting a starting point for the warning goal.
reaction: Fear is a plausible response to danger, though it does not yet explain how a warning is shared.
reason: Inspecting Fear will reveal how it can lead toward a warning without guessing between the remaining objects.
expectation: The report will show Fear's available partners and automatically combine it if only one operation is available.

effect: Fear can combine with either Sheltered oasis or Air, offering possible refuge and communication paths.
reaction: The two options suggest different responses to danger.
reason: Air could carry a vocal warning to another animal.
expectation: This may produce a warning call that others can hear.

reaction: The call makes the link between fear and communication clear.
reason: Inspecting Call will show what can receive or act on the warning, rather than guessing.
expectation: The report will show compatible partners and automatically combine Call if there is only one available operation.

effect: Call and Memory produced a Shared warning: companions can learn to associate the sound with danger, but the warning goal has not yet been reported complete.
reaction: The learned association makes the warning more meaningful than a sound alone.
reason: Inspecting Shared warning should reveal how another animal can act on it.
expectation: The report will show its available partners and automatically combine it if there is only one operation.

alternatives.reason: The oasis might provide a place to take refuge, but its connection to the warning is uncertain.

effect: Shared warning has no available partners, so it cannot yet complete the goal on its own.
reaction: That is slightly surprising; the warning exists but has not yet helped another life.
reason: Fear was also compatible with Sheltered oasis, which may provide the refuge needed to act on the warning.
expectation: This may produce a way to shelter from danger that can connect to the shared warning.

effect: Fear and the oasis produced Safety, a learned refuge that may let another animal act on the warning.
reaction: The shelter gives the warning a practical destination.
reason: Safety may connect with the shared warning to help another animal escape danger.
expectation: The warning and refuge may allow a companion to reach safety.

effect: Safety and Shared warning produced a Social group and completed the remaining goal: one animal can benefit from another's experience.
reaction: The result ties the warning to a practical benefit, while acknowledging that social life also involves conflict.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the learned path was most worthwhile: a remembered route lets an animal return to fruit it cannot yet see, giving memory a clear practical consequence.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting Shared warning was the least useful passage: it had no available partners at that point, even though the warning goal was still incomplete.

surprise.text: The warning alone did not complete the goal; a separately learned refuge had to be connected to it so another animal could benefit.

arbitrary.text: Returning fruit could not combine directly with Tree dwellers, despite seeming relevant to their finding food. The later memory-and-fruit combination made its purpose clearer.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how learned behaviour and social connections develop, especially given the chapter's caution that cooperation is not automatic.
